newsitem.title: UK: Britain ponders laser plan to defend troops - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain ponders laser plan to defend troops - paper.

text.p: Britain is considering developing a joint anti-ballistic missile defence system using lasers aboard modified Boeing 747s to protect troops deployed in overseas danger spots, the Guardian reported on Monday.
The newspaper, quoting government sources, said the cabinet could approve the new system at a special meeting later this month.
"Military commanders are pressing for a defensive system to combat the future threat to British forces overseas," the Guardian said.

It added that a Ministry of Defence study suggested Britain "buy in" components from the United States and cooperate with other NATO allies in a system which would be much more modest that the "Star Wars" plan first proposed by former U.S. president Ronald Reagan in 1983.
"The U.S. Air Force's airborne laser system, now being developed by the Seattle-based Boeing corporation, has emerged as the recommended solution," the newspaper said.
The lasers would shoot down incoming missiles in flight and be part of an anti-ballistic system which would also include early warning satellites and ship-based intercepter missiles.

"We have to be aware that in less than a decade we will be faced with the prospect of ballistic and cruise missiles from countries we don't see as stable or friendly reaching this country," a defence source told the Guardian.
